note: PRC-18. Nothing in this project exercised gamepad input before this file -- Joypad/JoyButton/JoyMotion returned zero hits across every .gd and every tools/*.py. This scenario drives dialog-skip, cursor and build+select through genuinely device-shaped InputEventJoypadMotion/InputEventJoypadButton events (the `gamepad` verb), not the action-shaped InputEventAction `press` already used elsewhere, proving LF-139's Input.parse_input_event() mechanism generalises to real controller input. First finding from building this: lf_build and lf_confirm share the SAME device-0 button-0 binding in project.godot, and dialog_view.gd's _unhandled_input() deliberately consumes lf_confirm with set_input_as_handled() while the anchor-01 boot brief (4 lines) is still showing -- 'so the gamepad button that advances a line does not also place an emplacement' (that file's own comment). A real player hits this too: the first button-0 presses page through the brief; only once it is fully dismissed does the same button reach the board. anchor-01's first slot is [2,3] and _step_cursor()'s first press with no cursor lands on slots[0] regardless of direction, so a single axis nudge deterministically parks the cursor there. Every gamepad action's effect is observable the FOLLOWING frame (same one-frame queueing delay as press/cursor).
